issue.description:
PROBLEM
The org secret-scanner (~/.local/bin/secret-scanner, run by the Claude Code PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop hook and the git pre-commit/pre-push hooks) and bead-rs's built-in scan (`bead doctor --scope secrets`, ruleset_version 3) disagree on the same checkpoint bytes. The org scanner blocks; bead-rs reports 0 blocking. `bead redact` only accepts bead-rs fingerprints, so an operator has NO in-tool way to clear what the org scanner flags. Auto-flush + ADR-018 auto-stage then put the flagged object file in the git index on every mutation, and every agent session started in that repo is blocked at Stop.

OBSERVED (declarative-config workspace, 2026-10-03)
- The org scanner flagged 9 lines per checkpoint object file: 7 generic-api-key, 2 basic-auth-uri. Each new auto-flush generation repeated all 9 (objects f3d03e4d…, e09e9b36…, bb3848bf…, 262329d7…).
- `bead doctor --scope secrets`: blocking_findings=0, advisory=868 (862 advisory-high-entropy-string, 6 advisory-keyword-assignment).
- I redacted the 2 live advisory-keyword-assignment findings (receipts d02200ea…, 8600eaba…; beads declarat-fc0b9e4f and the other live notes span). Afterwards the org scanner still flagged the same 9 object lines, and also forensic.jsonl:397, the rewritten record of declarat-fc0b9e4f. Redaction targeted a different span than the one the org scanner matches.
- Affected beads (object-file lines): declarat-1017298f, -148b000b, -3e7998ae, -5419d03d, -99c5c496, -bceed3fa, -f33465a0, -fc0b9e4f, plus a forensic event record at line 1863.
- A property-only classification (no values displayed) suggests these are false positives:
  - generic-api-key spans are 10-19 chars, lowercase plus punctuation, entropy 2.7-3.2. They look like identifiers or key names.
  - basic-auth-uri passwords are uppercase plus placeholder syntax (`${…}` or `<…>`), on git.ardenone.com clone URLs in CI-debugging bead notes.
  - This needs operator confirmation.

WANTED
1. Rule parity: bead-rs secret scan should detect at least what the org secret-scanner blocks on (generic-api-key and basic-auth-uri, with the same placeholder/allowlist semantics), or consume the org scanner's findings directly. Precedent: beadrs-374f9df6 (AWS secret key detection added for redaction).
2. `bead redact` needs to be able to target a finding the org scanner reports: by (path, line, rule) → resolved record/field/span, or by importing the org scanner's fingerprint.
3. An allowlist / acknowledged-false-positive path that the org scanner also honours, so a confirmed placeholder stops blocking Stop hooks without redacting useful bead text.
4. Consider not auto-staging a generation that the org scanner would reject (ADR-018 interaction).

ACCEPTANCE
- Re-running the org secret-scanner on a declarative-config checkpoint object produced after the fix yields zero findings, OR every finding is reachable by `bead redact --dry-run` or covered by a recorded acknowledgment.
- Conformance test: a fixture bead whose notes contain a generic-api-key / basic-auth-uri shaped string is detected by `bead doctor --scope secrets` with the same rule_id class as the org scanner.

Related: beadrs-4686ebdb (R038), beadrs-559d3bfe (BR-T18 NEEDLE remediation), beadrs-ef4fe443 (global secret-scanner hook interactions).
issue.notes:
Live reproduction: this bead's own description (written by claude-code 2026-10-03, contains no credential) is flagged by the org secret-scanner as generic-api-key at forensic.jsonl:46 and in each checkpoint object at line 46. bead doctor --scope secrets does not flag it, so bead redact cannot target it. Use this bead as the first conformance fixture.

Root cause (confirmed by bisecting the record through secret-scanner --stdin): description line 6, the bead doctor OBSERVED bullet. The rule matches the word secrets, then a backtick and colon, then the 19-char token for the blocking-findings count (snake_case name, equals sign, digit). The scanner reads that prose as keyword:value. So generic-api-key fires on ordinary diagnostic prose that has a keyword next to a key=value token. The org scanner's generic rule needs a stopword/entropy floor for snake_case identifiers. That is a second, org-scanner-side fix besides bead-rs parity.
2026-10-03 (claude-opus-interactive, operator: "complete these gaps in bead-rs"):
EVIDENCE (disposable workspace, sharded, synthetic AWS pair planted via --acknowledge-secret): bead redact removes a finding from beads.db, current/previous generations and forensic.jsonl, but one finding per call; each redaction changes the other findings' fingerprints (a pre-collected list fails 'not found'), and every intermediate publication re-emits the not-yet-redacted secrets (in sharded mode it rewrote forensic.jsonl containing one). 3 rounds of doctor->redact were needed for 3 findings. All-or-none batches = beadrs-ebec169c (codex-secret-gaps, in flight).
DESIGN for this bead (exact parity by construction, no second copy of the org rules): secret-scanner gains a value-free span mode (`--stdin --spans`: JSON rule + byte start/end per finding, never the bytes). bead-rs runs the configured org scanner over each live/retained field text, maps spans to (selector, field, start, end) and feeds them to the atomic batch redaction; doctor reports them as external findings. Scanner half done first in ~/secret-scanner (no overlap). bead-rs half waits for codex-secret-gaps' uncommitted redaction/checkpoint/scan work (41 files, active 2026-10-03 08:54 EDT) to land, to avoid conflicting edits.

Tests: tests/redact_all_blocking.rs (2) + external unit tests; full suite TMPDIR=/var/tmp with BEAD_TEST_ORG_SCANNER: 1601 passed, 0 failed, 6 ignored; fmt + clippy -D warnings clean. Installed on codinghome (~/.cargo/bin/bead, sha256 1229378523d7d5fcbb4395e57b863b80715c2d888b7a471f319f348548539879; previous kept as bead.pre-org-parity-20261003). Live check with parity on: bead doctor --scope secrets reports 0 blocking in commitgraph (26s), bead-rs, declarative-config, secret-scanner, nixos-asterisk. issue.description:
Plan: docs/plan/plan.md R042 item 1 (commit 75dc46a6; decision record beadrs-691c4fec). Operator-requested 2026-10-28. Evidence comes from a 2026-10-28 sweep of 98 bead-rs workspaces on codinghome (50,819 beads, copies deduplicated) and of transcripts from 2026-08-03 to 2026-10-28 (292,734 bead-related shell commands; regex baselines, not release claims).

Clean-room rule: amend the governing file under research/specs/ first, in its own commit, then implement only from it.

## Evidence
- `show` (text and JSON) and `why` omit the close reason, close time and closer. `query` (fields `close_reason`, `closed`) and `changes` (the `closed` event's `detail.reason`) already carry them.
- 1,662 transcript commands in 1,054 sessions looked for `close_reason` through `show` or `list`. Typical results: `jq '.close_reason'` returns null, and `Cannot index array with string "close_reason"`.
- Verified 2026-10-28 on bead 0.3.0: the keys of `bead show beadrs-5cdcd24d --json` include no closed_at, close_reason or closed_by. `bead why --id beadrs-5cdcd24d` prints the close time but not the reason.

## Scope
- Spec: define `closed_at` (RFC 3339 string or null), `closed_by` (actor string or null) and `close_reason` (string or null), all taken from the latest close. All three are null on an issue that was never closed, or that was reopened after its last close. Amend research/specs/agent-ergonomics-v1.md §2 or add research/specs/close-record-v1.md.
- `show` text: when closed, print a `Closed: <time> by <actor>` line and a `Reason:` block.
- `show --json` and every `list --json` row always carry the three keys. `list --fields` accepts them.
- `why`: the Timing section prints the closer and the reason.
- A redacted reason goes through the existing historical-redaction path and renders as `[REDACTED:bead-rs]`.
- `capabilities` advertises `close_record: true`, additive to native-v1 and the needle-v1 snapshot. `bead schema` reflects the keys.
- `closed_by` shows whatever actor the close event recorded, which today is mostly `system`. Capturing the real actor is beadrs-e167fde8, not this bead.

## Non-goals
No new storage and no change to close semantics.

## Acceptance
- Conformance tests cover:
  - close, then `show`, `list --json` and `why` expose the reason, time and actor;
  - reopen clears all three;
  - a second close shows the second record;
  - a redacted reason renders the marker;
  - a never-closed issue has nulls.
- Installed-binary help and schema tests are updated.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` pass on the pushed commit.
issue.title: Show the close reason, time and closer in show, list --json and why (R042.1)

issue.description:
Issues may declare normalized local resource keys. A claim atomically acquires every key its bead declares and excludes ready issues needing a key currently held; release, close, and lease expiry return keys. Readiness explanations gain a resource-conflict reason code. Scope is strictly one native store: workspace-local scheduling exclusion, never distributed locking, and naming/documentation must say so.

Adopted from the run-1 deferral after NEEDLE ADR-015 made bead-level serialization the accepted shared-checkout model.

Acceptance:
- resource-key validation, acquisition/release lifecycle, and migration specified
- claim excludes conflicting ready work atomically inside the claim transaction
- explain/why report a resource-conflict reason code
- documentation anchors scope to a single workspace

Refs: plan section 12 R031; ideas-ledger 2026-08-15 finalist 4 dossier; run-1 finalist 5.
issue.title: R031: Atomic resource locks
